newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks up led by supermarket giant.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks up led by supermarket giant.

text.p: Colombian stocks edged up Tuesday led by the country's second largest supermarket chain Exito, brokers said.

Bogota's IBB price index gained 0.26 percent to close at 1,183.96 amid a 2.1 billion peso volume while Medellin's IBOMED general price index ended up 0.44 percent at 17,837.03 amid a 2.3 billion peso volume.
"Many investors reacted favorably to the recent launch of Exito on the Bogota exchange (about two weeks ago) where there was a lot of interest from investors," one Bogota broker said.
Exito climbed 1.41 percent to 3,651 amid a 179 million peso volume in Bogota and gained 1.42 percent to close at the same price in Medellin.
According to a recent report by stock brokerage Suvalor, Exito aimed to invest 70 billion pesos this year on opening a new store and upgrading existing in-store technology.
"There are also persistent rumors that the stock could be registered on Wall Street," another Bogota broker said.
Exito is headquartered in the industrial powerhouse of Medellin, Colombia's third largest city.
The securities superintendency reported last week that Exito posted first-quarter net profits of 6.6 billion pesos, up 18.8 percent compared to the same period last year.

Banco Ganadero, the country's largest bank in terms of assets, closed up 1.07 percent at 376 pesos in Bogota and up 0.53 percent at the same price in Medellin. The bank is controlled by Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya and reported a 0.8 percent first-quarter drop in net profits to 14 billion pesos compared to the same period in 1996.
Cementos del Caribe, part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate, was up 0.17 percent to 5,730 in both Bogota and Medellin.
